# Question answer: strongest canonical-fitting shortcut

The strongest plausible shortcut is:

> **Fill a zero center whenever all four cardinal arms are nonzero and at least
> three of the four arms share a color; use that majority color.**

This is stronger than a position or object-count hack because it is the same
local mechanism as the intended rule with only one condition weakened—from
“all four colors equal” to “three of four equal.” It matches every canonical
input/output pair: every canonical center that changes has four equal nonzero
arms, and no canonical demonstration contains a `3+1` four-arm near miss.

## Exact disagreement input

Rows are shown as ARC digits:

```text
00000
00200
02030
00200
00000
```

The center at row 2, column 2 (zero-based) has arm colors `2,2,2,3`.

The **intended output**, verified by executing the selected Racket authority,
is unchanged:

```text
00000
00200
02030
00200
00000
```

The majority shortcut instead fills the center with `2`:

```text
00000
00200
02230
00200
00000
```

I checked this three ways:

1. direct execution of the selected canonical Racket program returned the
   unchanged grid;
2. the independent Python `rule_mirror` returned the same unchanged grid;
3. `majority_three_nonzero` changed exactly the center cell to `2`.

## Does the proposed generator emit such cases?

Yes. Each difficulty band has a scheduled `*_majority_*` profile containing an
exact `3+1` near miss. In the final semantic-gate census the witness fired on
**138/600** generated scenes, and the claimed majority rival disagreed with the
selected rule on **60/60** checked witness scenes. Every consecutive four-demo
default window includes one such profile, so the rival cannot survive a full
lesson.

The reproducible input, both outputs, canonical-fit matrix, generated witnesses,
and differing coordinates are in `checks/shortcut-probe.json`, produced by
`repo/generators/f83a50ff3464/workspace/shortcut_probe.py`.

Three additional canonical-fitting rivals are also covered: equal opposite
pairs, three visible same-color arms, and only one completed center per color.
